findings.location: Table 1, 'Schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorders' block (7 diagnostic-category rows)

findings.notes: The seven ICD-10 psychiatric diagnostic categories are presented as a partition of the 2830-patient sample, but the counts total 2840 - ten patients more than the stated N. The accompanying percentages are each individually consistent with a denominator of 2830 (80.32 = 2273/2830, 11.45 = 324/2830, and so on), so the percentage column and the count column were computed against the same N; the excess sits in the counts themselves. The likeliest innocent explanation is that ten patients carry two SSD diagnoses and are counted in two rows, but the paper's inclusion criteria state a single ICD-10 F20-F29 category per patient, so this warrants clarification. Rests only on figures the paper prints.

consequence.explanation: Affects only the descriptive statement that Schizophrenia (F20) accounted for 80.32% of the sample; no inferential result in Table 2 or Table 3 depends on this partition.

findings.location: Table 1, 'Binary comorbidity (Top 10)' block, against the Results text
findings.quote: There were 470 cases with two CVD comorbidities (16.60%), with the most common combination being primary hypertension and sequelae of cerebrovascular disease (6.71%)
findings.reproduction: metascience summation-batch --rows '[{"values":[190,188,158,123,103,93,92,74,70,56],"expected_sum":470,"decimals":0,"tolerance":0,"description":"Table 1 top-10 binary comorbidity counts vs stated 470"}]'
findings.notes: Only the TOP TEN binary combinations are listed, so their subtotal must be at most the stated number of patients with exactly two CVD comorbidities. It is 1147 against a stated 470 - more than double. The first three rows alone (190 + 188 + 158 = 536) already exceed 470. Under the 'exactly two comorbidities' reading printed in the text this is arithmetically impossible; under the alternative reading, that these rows count every patient carrying that PAIR regardless of how many other CVDs they have, the numbers reconcile but are then inconsistent with the 'Single comorbidity' block, whose top-ten subtotal (1734) does sit below its stated total of 1893. The two blocks cannot both use the same definition. Severity held at suspicious rather than impossible because the ambiguity is definitional and either block could be the one mislabelled.

consequence.explanation: Affects the Results claims that 470 patients (16.60%) had two comorbidities and that primary hypertension + sequelae of cerebrovascular disease was the commonest pair at 6.71%; the LCA and regression results do not use these counts.

findings.notes: At their printed two-decimal precision neither value is expressible as an integer count over 2830: 1893/2830 rounds to 66.89 and 470/2830 rounds to 16.61. Both become consistent at one decimal, so the parsimonious reading is that the authors computed to one decimal and padded a trailing zero to match the two-decimal style used elsewhere. I have recorded this as SUSPICIOUS rather than the tool's IMPOSSIBLE verdict because the discrepancy is one unit in the last printed digit and is fully explained by that padding; it is a presentation defect, not an unreproducible number. Both counts (1893, 470) and the denominator (2830) are stated by the paper, so the check rests on no assumed bound.

consequence.explanation: No claim changes; the underlying counts are correct and the error is confined to the second decimal place of two descriptive percentages.

Note this is a per-cell check with the p-value supplied from the adjacent column, which is why it was run directly rather than through check_table - check_table types each cell in isolation and cannot pair an estimate with a p-value held in a different column.

findings.notes: These five cells cannot be evaluated at all: an odds ratio of exactly zero, or an interval whose lower bound is zero, has no logarithm, and check_estimate_ci correctly refuses rather than returning a verdict. The refusal is itself the finding. Table 2 supplies the cause and it is not a transcription error - these are structural zeros. No patient aged 70+ and no widowed patient falls in the heart failure class (both cells print 0 (0.00)); only 6 of 375 heart-failure patients are from Northern China. This is (quasi-)complete separation, under which the maximum-likelihood estimate diverges and the Wald interval is meaningless. The interval '1.88 (0, 31465.17)' spanning five orders of magnitude, and '0.00 (0.00, 0.00)' carrying p < 0.001, are the visible symptoms. The paper reports these alongside well-identified estimates with no caveat and no penalised-likelihood alternative.

consequence.explanation: Supports the Results claim that patients over 26 and in other marital statuses were 'less likely to have comorbidities associated with the Heart Failure group' (OR < 1.00), which rests partly on estimates that are numerically degenerate rather than estimated.

findings.location: Abstract and Results 'Proportion of diseases and comorbidity patterns', against the Table 2 column headers
findings.quote: four distinct comorbidity patterns were identified based on their dominant characteristics: low-risk CVDs (47.86%), primary hypertension (30.15%), heart failure (12.99%), and cardiac valve and vascular disorders (8.99%)
findings.reproduction: metascience summation-batch --rows '[{"values":[47.86,30.15,12.99,8.99],"expected_sum":100,"decimals":2,"description":"abstract LCA class percentages"},{"values":[1293,937,375,225],"expected_sum":2830,"decimals":0,"tolerance":0,"description":"Table 2 class n"}]'
findings.notes: Two different partitions of the same 2830 patients are presented without being reconciled. Each is internally sound - the percentages total 100 and the counts total 2830, both verified - but they are not the same partition, and the largest class differs by roughly two percentage points. This is very likely the ordinary and legitimate distinction between a latent class model's estimated mixing proportions and the counts obtained by assigning each patient to their most probable class; those two quantities do differ in any LCA. The paper never says which figure is which, and the abstract's percentages are the ones a reader will carry away. Left INDETERMINATE deliberately: I did not compute the ratio of the Table 2 counts to N, so I am not asserting a specific size for the gap, only that the two sets are presented as though interchangeable and are not.

consequence.explanation: Affects the abstract's headline prevalence figures for the four comorbidity patterns, which do not correspond to the class sizes used in every subsequent analysis.

findings.quote: All tests were 2-sided, with a significance level set at 0.05.

inputs.text: Results and Discussion sections, including the eight Table 2 chi-squared values and the odds ratios quoted in prose

findings.reproduction: metascience statcheck --text "<Results and Discussion body text>"
findings.notes: statcheck ran successfully and found nothing to verify. This is a property of the paper's reporting style, not a tool failure: the χ2 values in Table 2 are printed without degrees of freedom and with asterisk markers instead of p-values, and the regression results are given as bare odds ratios without any test statistic. None of this matches the APA grammar statcheck parses. The consequence is that statcheck provides no independent corroboration here - the χ2 verification in this review came instead from recomputing each statistic from its own contingency table, which is a stronger check.

consequence.explanation: No claim is affected; the check simply had no applicable input.

findings.reproduction: metascience multiplicity --family-label 'Table 3 psychotropic medication coefficients, Heart failure class' --tests '[{"id":"halo_inj","p_value":0.001},{"id":"risperidone","p_value":0.002},{"id":"olanzapine","p_value":0.011},{"id":"clozapine","p_value":0.037},{"id":"aripiprazole","p_value":0.007},{"id":"amisulpride","p_value":0.016},{"id":"dexzopiclone","p_value":0.022}]'
findings.notes: INDETERMINATE on tooling grounds, not on the paper. multiplicity_report returned n_tests = 0 with the note 'no uncorrected tests' on two separate attempts - once with correction_applied and p_is_threshold supplied per test, once with a plain list of exact p-values only - so its `tests` argument was evidently not parsed into the list the tool expects. No corrected thresholds or surviving-claim counts were produced and I am therefore asserting none. What can be stated without the tool, from the paper alone: Table 3 contains 51 predictor rows x 3 outcome classes = 153 Wald tests, Table 2 contains 8 univariate tests, the Statistical analysis section declares alpha = 0.05 and states no correction of any kind, and several claims that reach the abstract and discussion rest on coefficients with p between 0.01 and 0.05 (amisulpride 0.029, clozapine 0.037, dexzopiclone 0.022, lorazepam 0.019, risperidone 0.049). Quantifying how many survive correction requires a working run of this tool.

consequence.explanation: Cannot be determined without a successful multiplicity run; flagged so the editorial stage can re-attempt rather than treat the family as corrected.

findings.notes: PRESENT BUT UNREADABLE, which is different from absent. The file extracted successfully but returned 1,114,127 characters across 33,652 lines, exceeding what the harness can deliver in one result; it was spilled to a temporary file. Reading it back by line offset would mean sampling rows rather than extracting the tables, and a check built on a sampled table is worse than no check, so I did not do so. This is the single largest coverage gap in this review and it is a consequential one: eTable 5 holds the LCA model-selection statistics (BIC and the other fit indices) that justify the four-class solution, and eTables 2-4 hold the full single/binary/ternary comorbidity distributions that would settle the Table 1 binary-and-ternary discrepancy recorded above. Re-running this extraction with paging enabled at the tool level, or converting the workbook to CSV per sheet, would close it.

consequence.explanation: The four-class LCA solution and the comorbidity-count distributions are unverified; eTables 2-4 would likely resolve whether the Table 1 binary/ternary blocks count exclusive or overlapping combinations.

findings.reproduction: No tool applies; recorded by direct reading of the Data availability statement.
findings.notes: Recorded for completeness rather than as a red flag. The paper does not claim the data are included or openly deposited, so this is not the 'state-but-withhold' pattern; identifiable psychiatric inpatient records from three named hospitals carry a genuine ethical constraint, and an ethics approval number is given. The practical consequence for this review is only that the Table 1 count discrepancy and the degenerate Table 3 estimates cannot be resolved against the underlying records.

consequence.explanation: No claim is affected; noted because it bounds what any external check can resolve.

figures.label: Fig. 1

unchecked.reason: The per-indicator conditional probabilities for 50 CVD categories across 4 classes exist only as bars in this figure. The text gives summary values only ('conditional probabilities < 0.25', 'conditional probability = 1', 'conditional probabilities: 0.43-0.58'), so the great majority of the plotted values appear nowhere in text or table. Values read off a chart carry figure-pixel provenance and are barred from the exact-arithmetic checks, so no check was attempted.

unchecked.location: Fig. 1, network map node sizes and edge weights
unchecked.reason: Node sizes encode disease proportions and edge thickness encodes co-occurrence frequency; neither is printed numerically. The underlying proportions are said to be in eTable 1 of Supplement 2, which could not be read (see above).

Deviation from the standard route, recorded deliberately. Tables 1 and 2 are pure count-and-percentage grids whose entire arithmetic (35 count sums with tolerance 0, plus 5 percentage columns) was checked exhaustively by check_summation_batch, which check_table does not do. For Table 3 the decisive check pairs each OR/CI cell with its p-value from a SEPARATE column; check_table types cells in isolation and cannot make that pairing, so it would have tested only log-midpoint symmetry. check_estimate_ci was run directly on 21 cells with the p-value supplied instead. The cost is that the remaining 132 OR/CI cells did not receive the weaker symmetry-only check.

unchecked.location: Table 2, 'Fisher**' entries for the typical antipsychotic, atypical antipsychotic, anxiolytic and mood stabiliser blocks
unchecked.reason: Four of the twelve univariate tests report 'Fisher**' with no test statistic and no exact p-value, so there is nothing to recompute. The contingency tables are present, but Fisher's exact test on tables of up to 12 x 4 with N = 2830 is not what any available tool computes, and recomputing them as chi-squared would test a different hypothesis than the one reported.
No standard deviation, standard error, median or IQR is reported for age, and the analysis uses banded age groups throughout. With no dispersion figure, no granularity or dispersion check applies.

21 cells were checked with check_estimate_ci, selected to cover every abstract-level claim plus a spread of results near alpha; all passed. The remaining 132 were not individually tested. No batch form of check_estimate_ci exists, and paging the 427 table cells to feed check_table would have bought only the weaker symmetry-only check (see the parse_cells_typed entry above).

Not run. Its three stated purposes did not apply: extract_xml flagged no table as alignment_uncertain and none as image_only, and both figure captions were recovered in full from the XML body text. The residual gap is that values plotted only in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 were not read off the artwork, which is recorded separately above.

The choice of four classes therefore could not be verified, and it determines every result in Tables 2 and 3.
